$comment: RFC-0069. An agent from idea to a launch a person signed. The threat model is the gate because a path from untrusted content to private data and out is fixed in the design, not in the config; the launch gate is human because only the owner can accept the residual risk and the eval result together.
name: ship-agent
description: Take an AI agent from an idea to a launch a person signed: the loop spec with its exit criteria and cap, the spend caps per stage, a threat model where every lethal-trifecta path has an architectural fix, an eval harness with its pass bar set before the first run, and a review of the real agent configuration before launch, with a gate that sends the design back when a path to exfiltration stays open. Use when the user says "we're building an agent", "design and ship this agent safely", "run the ship-agent loop", or wants an agent taken from design to launch with its risks and evals settled.

stages.intent: Specify the loop: its job and observable done, the generate-verify-gate cycle, the cap, the human gates at irreversible steps, and, when the work fans out, the subagents and their contracts.
Set the model tier, token cap and abort rule per stage of the design, with cost per outcome as the governing number.
Threat-model the design's capabilities against the lethal trifecta and judge whether every unsafe path has an architectural fix.
Design the golden set, grading and metric, with the pass bar and regression gate fixed before the first run, and the threat model's attacks as adversarial cases.
Once the agent is built: review its real configuration against the threat model, put the eval result beside the pass bar, and the owner decides the launch.
